record.paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
record.original_question: Let X be a T0 space and Y a strong d-space. Is the function space Top0(X,Y), consisting of continuous maps X to Y and equipped with the pointwise convergence topology, itself a strong d-space?

evidence.quote: Question 8.11. Let X be a T0 space and Y a strong d-space. Is the function space Top0 (X, Y ) equipped with the pointwise convergence topology a strong d-space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Definitions. A topological space is T0 if for any two distinct points there is an open set containing exactly one of them. For a T0 space Z, let ≤ denote the specialization order, defined by x ≤ y iff x ∈ cl({y}). A subset D ⊆ Z is directed if it is nonempty and every two elements of D have an upper bound in D (with respect to ≤). Write ↑x = {z ∈ Z : x ≤ z} and, for A ⊆ Z, ↑A = ⋃_{a∈A} ↑a; a set is saturated if it equals its upward closure.

A T0 space Z is called a strong d-space if for every directed subset D ⊆ Z and every open set U ⊆ Z such that ↑D ⊆ U (where the upward closure is taken in the specialization order), there exists d ∈ D with ↑d ⊆ U.

For T0 spaces X and Y, let Top0(X,Y) denote the set of all continuous maps from X to Y. Equip Top0(X,Y) with the topology of pointwise convergence, namely the subspace topology inherited from the product space Y^X (with the product topology of |X| copies of Y).

Question. Let X be an arbitrary T0 space and let Y be a strong d-space. Must the function space Top0(X,Y), with the topology of pointwise convergence, also be a strong d-space?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g. on S*-well-filtered spaces and strong d-spaces, 2025–2026) addresses function spaces in the Isbell topology, where preservation can fail, but does not resolve the pointwise-convergence case for strong d-spaces. No source located that settles the question for Top0(X,Y) with the pointwise convergence topology, so it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: S*-well-filtered spaces and d*-spaces (arXiv 2601.11281)
status_evidence.snippet: if Y is an S*-well-filtered space, the function space TOP(X,Y) equipped with the Isbell topology may not be an S*-well-filtered space
status_evidence.claim: Related recent work treats function-space preservation problems but only for the Isbell topology, not for the pointwise convergence topology in the strong d-space setting.

status_evidence.title: Strongly well-filtered spaces and strong d-spaces
status_evidence.snippet: every strongly well-filtered space is a strong d-space
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature on strong d-spaces continues to investigate their properties but does not appear to resolve the pointwise-convergence function space question.
